summary: A steel lookout built near Marienville in 1921; in 1952 it was reportedly dismantled and moved to Chestnut Ridge, Fayette County, and its current state is unconfirmed.

facts.design: steel (maker not named in the sources read)
facts.status_note: Dismantled in 1952 and moved to Chestnut Ridge, Fayette County. No source read confirms whether it still stands there, and none places a tower at Marienville after 1952.

events.note: First fire tower in that section, steel, 60 feet, near Marienville, per an October 1921 newspaper item.
The Marienville towerman is named in a 1924 item describing the towerman watching two bears near the tower.
Dismantled and re-erected at Chestnut Ridge, Fayette County, per 1952 sources. The 1952 item describes an 80-foot tower there, replacing Banning Knob.
Registered January 2, 2026 as US 1814, PA 74, nominated by Coltin Carr.

corrections.why: The 1952 items say the tower was dismantled and moved from near Marienville to Chestnut Ridge, Fayette County. No source read places a tower at Marienville after 1952, and the Register entry does not mention the move.
The 1921 items say the tower is steel and do not name a maker. No source read names Aermotor for the Marienville tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register entry names the Marienville tower (registered 2026), but the 1952 items say it was moved. The record now reads relocated, because the 1952 items are specific and the Register does not mention a move. Whether the Chestnut Ridge tower still stands is not confirmed.
The 1921 item says 60 feet and the 1952 item describes an 80-foot tower on Chestnut Ridge. The 18.3 m figure is kept for the 1921 tower and the two are not assumed to be the same structure.

notes_for_editor: Record status standing and design Aermotor do not hold up in the sources read; corrections proposed. Do not conflate the Fayette County Chestnut Ridge with the Chestnut Ridge tower near Frenchville in Clearfield County (Moshannon State Forest), which a search snippet describes as an 80-foot new tower; that snippet was not read and is not cited. The NHLR registration of January 2, 2026 does not mention the 1952 move and may be out of date. The relocation rests on 1952 newspaper items reprinted on one lookout-history site. The current state of the Fayette tower is unconfirmed. No photos added. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the story no longer gives the 1924 towerman a gender, since the item does not; the agency and the 1921 build year are now in the evidence list, both taken from the NHLR page.
